full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Third Court, Dacca dated 29.2.1980 in Title Appeal No. 141 of 1979 affirming those passed by the learned Munsif, Third Court, Dacca dated 28.6.1979 in Title Suit No. 409 of 1976 and arises out of a suit for declaration that acceptance of the letter of resignation tendered by the plaintiff is void, illegal and without any lawful authority and has no legal effect. 

 4. Both the courts below have held that once a resignation is tendered it cannot be withdrawn by a subsequent letter. It was further held that since the letter of resignation was handed over to the Despatch Section the plaintiff could not take the same back and the taking of some copies out of the despatch section cannot help the plaintiff petitioner because of the fact that taking back of a letter without permission of the authority was irregular and unauthorized and in the normal course of business it should be treated as has been dispatched to the proper authority. It has also been found by the Courts below that the order passed against the plaintiff was rightly and legally passed and as such the plaintiff was not entitled to any relief whatsoever in the suit or in the appeal resulting there. Hence this application against the said concurrent judgment and decrees. Mr. Asrarul Hossein, with Mr. Walla Rena Chowdhury, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the petitioner and Mr. Tofailur Rahman, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the defendants opposite parties. 

 6. Mr. Tofailur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the defendant opposite parties supports the judgments and decrees passed by the courts below and contends that the courts below were right in holding that the plaintiff petitioner was not entitled to any relief in view of the fact that he has tendered his resignation and since resignation has been tendered even though effective at a letter dated that cannot be subsequently withdrawn. 

 8. For that reason it was recommended In the report that the petitioner should be allowed to continue in his service and posted at some other place. After that the matter was sent to the law officer for legal advise. The law officer also gave his opinion to the effect that much before acceptance of the resignation letter without the original copy, the petitioner has withdrawn his resignation, as such he should be allowed to continue in service. Inspire of this on 19.11.74 he was informed by the secretary of the Bangladesh Jute Industries Corporation that his resignation dated 16.9.1974 has been accepted With immediate effect. All these facts, circumstances tend to show that the petitioner has been victimized for his appearing before the President's Vigilance Team as has been found in the report of the Enquiry Inspection done by the BJIC. Even after 12.10.74 no cognizance was taken of the resignation letter. But all on a sudden a copy of the resignation was obtained from the Accounts and on it was recommended by the General Manager that the petitioner's resignation should be accepted with immediate effect in the interest of the mill. It is strange that after 12.10.74 when the petitioner was working to the satisfaction of his superiors and was recommended for higher grade, all on a sudden his services was found to the detrimental to the Mill. This itself is a glaring example of high handedness of the authority in dealing with the case of the petitioner. It transpires that certain charges were also formed against him but those charges could not be substantiated and he was found not guilty. All these tend to show that the order of acceptance of the resignation was malafide. The petitioner though submitted resignation letter has withdrawn it before the date from which it was to be effective. The petitioner had a right to withdraw it before it became effective. As such the findings of the courts below that the petitioner could not withdraw the resignation letter in view of the fact that he has filed the resignation letter in his office and there is no illegality on the part of the defendant opposite parties in accepting the resignation tendered by the petitioner cannot be maintained. The order accepting the resignation is malafide. In that view of the matter the Rule is made absolute and the judgments and decrees passed by the courts below are set aside and suit is decreed.
